generation_budget.revision_guidance: Inspect the current candidate and choose a focused edit or fresh generation from the actual defect and the user's intent.

communication_intent.audience_question: Show a controlled source-to-client flow and the responsibilities, evidence records and rejection feedback needed to operate it.
communication_intent.dominant_message: Keep expert ownership at every release

information_structure.description: Show a controlled source-to-client flow and the responsibilities, evidence records and rejection feedback needed to operate it.

required_content.text: A controlled path from permissioned evidence to approved client work.

required_content.heading: SHARED CONTROLS
items: One register records defects, owners and disposition.
Platform team maintains access controls and audit logs.

required_content.heading: PILOT MEASUREMENT
items: Compare 20 paired tasks with baseline time logs.
Verify claim samples and record expert review effort.

required_content.label: RELEASE RULE
required_content.message: No client use without expert and engagement-lead sign-off.

evidence: Host-authored illustrative planning model. The preserved work/planning-assumptions.json carries the exact calculation assumptions.
assumptions: Northstar Advisory is fictional. Capacity equivalent is not revenue or cash savings.
The pilot measures one comparable research task per engagement, so 20 tasks correspond to 20 engagements.
The 95% sampled-claim gate does not replace expert verification and approval of each client release.
avoid: Any generated header, footer, company label, page number, shared-frame rule or repeated source-note strip.
Independent changes to recurring title size, font family or decision-band treatment.
Icons that repeat a label without improving recognition or scanability.
visual_obligations: Generate only the 1920 by 960 substantive canvas at exactly 2:1 aspect ratio. The runtime adds the separate inherited frame.
Use native-friendly text, tables, chart geometry and continuous directed relationships where the content requires them.
Follow the shared deck design. The five pages vary their evidence structures while recurring roles remain consistent.
Use one coherent icon family across the source, draft, review, and release stages.
explicit_user_visual_requirements: Georgia claim title at 64 px regular on every page, with no per-page shrinking.
Arial subtitle 32 px regular, body 28 px regular, section labels 28 px bold and table text 24 px.
Every decision band uses pale orange #FFF5ED fill, orange #FD5108 label and left bar, black message, and no surrounding border.
Place all necessary page-specific qualifications in the substantive content. Shared frame wording is excluded from image generation.

style.visual_language: Consulting editorial presentation language: purposeful orange, black and white foundation, precise serif/sans hierarchy, clear movement, deliberate asymmetry when useful, disciplined negative space, strong scale contrast, thin neutral rules, and only a small number of coherent visual treatments on one slide.
style.whitespace: intentional and confidence-building; preserve the selected density while using spacing and scale to reduce visual noise

non_negotiable_design.icon_slot_rule: For every icon, reserve a visually unambiguous bounded slot that protects its room from surrounding content. The icon may have no designed surface or may sit on a profile-approved background surface. When there is no designed surface, a subtle generation-only boundary may mark the slot for localization; that boundary is scaffolding, not a decorative container and is not reconstructed downstream. When the icon sits on a larger colored panel/card and no distinct icon tile is intended, the downstream reconstruction should keep the icon background transparent rather than turning the scaffold into a white box.

profile.name: Consulting
profile.purpose: Create disciplined, evidence-rich executive slides with clear arguments, precise hierarchy and restrained moments of emphasis.

rules: Lead with core orange when colour is needed, but use it purposefully as an accent rather than a routine full-slide fill.
Use white and black as the foundation. Add approved orange or grey tints when more colour is needed.
Do not use red or rose as ordinary presentation colours; they are limited-use illustration colours.
Functional status colours are functional cues only and are not brand accents.
Ordinary text is black or white. Orange text is reserved for selected numbers, data visualisation, or call-to-action treatment.
Use Georgia for slide headlines and quotes.
Use Arial for sub-headlines, body copy, introductions, labels, and large data numbers.
Do not use italics.
Do not apply tracking.
Use black text on white, warm accents, restrained gradients, and profile tints. White text on the lead orange requires sufficiently large display text; use 18 pt or larger.

Use the PowerPoint hierarchy leading as a guide: headlines 100%, sub-headlines and introductions 120%, body 150%, large data numbers 100%, quotes and quote labels 120%, and labels/calls to action 100%.

primary_gradient.purpose: Create selected moments of impact and momentum, not routine decoration.
primary_gradient.reconstruction_without_canonical_asset: Preserve the accepted generated gradient as a raster visual region or canonical supplied asset. Do not invent proprietary editable gradient stops that are not specified by the source standard.
rules: Do not rotate, flip, or arbitrarily crop a directional warm gradient treatment.
Do not create unrelated new gradients.
Use a warm gradient sparingly for deliberate impact, and keep standard data visualisation solid and restrained.
For standard PowerPoint data visualisation, use solid warm accents and grey tints with one clear lead colour.
When one data point matters most, highlight it with core orange against grey tints.
When several data points have equal weight, use a monochromatic orange-tint sequence before grey tints.
Use core orange for the highest-value end of an orange heatmap.
Use Georgia for chart titles and Arial for data, category labels, and large number callouts.
Do not use gradients in standard data visualisation.
Tables may use core orange for a header row or column and approved grey tints for alternating rows.

icons.asset_policy: Use Remix Icon as the coherent generic icon source when its run switch is enabled. Wikimedia Commons is reserved for exact logo or public-media candidates. Inspect every selected external asset and keep it in the run cache with provenance. Any fetched asset remains subject to the resolved profile treatment rules.

public_showcase_override.activation: Enable each required source independently under session remote_sources.
public_showcase_override.pair_policy: Retrieve a Remix line/fill pair before generation. Host Agent selects one variant per icon_treatment_group after inspecting the approved generated slide.
public_showcase_override.identity_boundary: Generic icons are supporting communication symbols only. Never use one as a logo, trademark, or brand identity. Wikimedia Commons results are candidates whose exact identity, license, attribution, and trademark constraints still require Agent review.

icons.slot_policy: Every icon has an explicit reserved slot for generation and measurement. A faint generation-only boundary may mark a bare icon slot for localization, but that boundary is scaffolding, not a decorative container, and must not be reconstructed. Only a positively judged intentional background surface may be reconstructed. When an icon sits directly on a larger colored panel/card and the visible white box merely isolates/localizes the glyph, prefer no reconstructed slot surface so the icon background remains transparent and inherits the surrounding panel colour.
icons.coherence_policy: Assign one treatment to each local peer icon or pictogram group. The host Agent chooses the peer grouping and one treatment id for that group. Reconstruction applies that treatment coherently while preserving each selected Remix glyph's geometry.

surface_geometry_policy.description: A flat light background field may sit behind an icon only when the accepted design clearly intends a real icon surface. It is a background surface, not a decorative badge or holding shape. Do not add circles, pills, outlines, extra marks, or scaffold borders around the icon. When the surrounding panel already provides the background, omit the icon surface and keep the icon background transparent.

avoid: stretching or distorting an icon
recolouring an exact Consulting SVG away from its canonical black or tangerine-to-orange artwork
arbitrary decorative circles, pills, badges, or holding shapes around an icon
adding extra marks or lines to the icon artwork
using icon background fills other than white, #FFF5ED, or #F5F7F8 in the Consulting profile
mixing several unrelated icon styles on one slide
reconstructing a localization/scaffold border as a real icon box or outline
using a white knockout tile when the intended background should be the surrounding colored panel

asset_vocabulary.policy: For Consulting generation, reusable semantic assets are selected upstream and shown together in one approved context sheet. The sheet contains selected visual references, component previews, retrieved candidate assets, and current-chat/user uploads. Canonical identity files remain authoritative downstream. The image model may also create profile-governed novel illustrations when they materially improve communication; these are a distinct class, not substitutes for logos or known assets, and are handled explicitly during reconstruction.
asset_vocabulary.review_rule: Every meaningful semantic visual must either map to an approved upstream asset/reference class, be native presentation geometry, be an explicitly allowed raster role, or be classified as a profile-permitted novel illustration. Reject decorative or off-profile novel visuals.

novel_illustrations.guidance: Prefer native presentation geometry and approved assets. Allow a small number of semantically necessary illustrative visuals when they materially clarify a concept or create a justified narrative moment. Creative/conceptual slides may use more expressive illustration; compliance, regulatory, operating, or data-dense slides should use little or none. Do not add decorative novelty merely to fill space.

reasoning_principles: Start from the audience question and the one belief, understanding, or decision the slide should create.
Treat the slide as an argument unit, not a container for topics.
Distinguish claim, evidence, context, qualification, and recommendation when those roles exist.
Preserve sequence, comparison, hierarchy, causality, dependency, contribution, and parallelism when supported by the content.
Do not invent completeness, causality, or evidence that the source material does not support.
Use MECE only as a diagnostic when the content is intended to be a complete decomposition.
visual_principles: Create movement by guiding the eye deliberately; use asymmetry when it improves flow rather than defaulting to a centered or rigidly uniform composition.
Let content breathe. Use intentional spacing and clear hierarchy to reduce visual noise while preserving the user's selected density.
Create moments of impact sparingly through scale contrast, a purposeful orange accent, a selected gradient moment, or a strong data callout.
Let semantic relationships drive visual relationships and make dependencies immediately legible.
Use emphasis in proportion to argumentative importance rather than giving every group equal visual weight.
Keep colour application disciplined: one strong orange-led system with approved tints and neutrals is more Consulting-like than a multicolour palette.

When photography is used, prefer professional, tech-forward, authentic human situations, focused compositions, candid collaboration, warm natural tones, and imagery that feels real rather than filtered or synthetic.
writing_principles: Prefer a specific conclusion-led title when the evidence supports a conclusion; otherwise use a precise structural title.
Keep supporting copy economical, clear, and decision-relevant.
Use direct language and avoid generic framing, filler, and repeated labels.
review_questions: Can the audience identify the main takeaway quickly?
Does the slide unmistakably use the resolved Consulting orange, black, white, tint, and typography system rather than approximate lookalikes?
Are Georgia and Arial assigned to the correct headline versus supporting roles, with no accidental italics or coloured ordinary body text?
Do icons use coherent Consulting-inspired foreground/background treatments at each peer level, avoiding accidental black-versus-gradient mixing inside one visual group?
Does the layout create purposeful movement, breathing room, and moments of impact without contradicting the selected density?
If a chart or table is present, does it use one warm lead colour with restrained grey support unless a more expressive treatment was explicitly chosen?
If a gradient is used, does it create a real moment of impact and remain consistent with the resolved palette?
Can every meaningful icon, pictogram, logo, photograph, illustration, or other semantic visual in the candidate be mapped to a selected upstream asset description?
anti_patterns: generic SaaS dashboard aesthetic
off-brand red/orange palette approximations
ordinary body text in accent colours
multiple unrelated accent colours next to each other
arbitrary decorative icon circles, pills, or badges
mixing black, white, solid orange, and gradient icons without a coherent slide-level treatment
using a warm gradient as generic decoration
using gradients in standard PowerPoint charts
overly uniform equal-card layouts when the argument has unequal importance
content dump without a governing message
invented semantic visuals that were not retrieved/selected upstream

generation_guidance: Use the substantive canvas actively with compact, well-structured information groups and strong alignment.
Avoid large isolated blank regions unless they clearly serve hierarchy, pacing, or emphasis.
Prefer expanding, aligning, or redistributing meaningful content before adding decoration.
Keep spacing disciplined and readable; dense does not mean cramped.
visual_review_guidance: Inspect the whole canvas for avoidable dead zones or lopsided whitespace.
Reject a composition that feels under-filled for the selected density even if individual components look good.
Preserve breathing room inside groups while using the overall slide area efficiently.
Judge empty regions by whether they support the argument, hierarchy, or pacing rather than by the semantic type of the nearby element.

style_direction.intent: Dense, readable executive content with Georgia claim titles, Arial supporting roles and one coherent decision-band treatment.
style_direction.freedom: Vary the meaningful information layout. Preserve the shared visual roles and body-only canvas.

communication_roles: Make the four operating stages recognizable before the reader enters the responsibility matrix
icons.decision: Use one coherent icon family across the source, draft, review, and release stages.

communication_roles: Provide editable information structures for the slide evidence
components.decision: Use native tables, charts, connectors, and geometry because the current evidence structures are specific to this argument.

communication_roles: Preserve the shared title, typography, decision band, and deck rhythm
visual_references.decision: Use the shared deck design as the primary authority. Later pages may use the accepted opening only for style calibration.

selected_visual_references.reason: Align the shared Georgia claim-title scale, Arial supporting typography and pale-orange decision band with orange label and black message. Use this page only as a visual style reference. Preserve the current page facts and choose its own chart, workflow, matrix or investment layout. Do not copy the opening content or its three-column composition.

asset_vocabulary_policy.policy: For Consulting generation, reusable semantic assets are selected upstream and shown together in one approved context sheet. The sheet contains selected visual references, component previews, retrieved candidate assets, and current-chat/user uploads. Canonical identity files remain authoritative downstream. The image model may also create profile-governed novel illustrations when they materially improve communication; these are a distinct class, not substitutes for logos or known assets, and are handled explicitly during reconstruction.
asset_vocabulary_policy.review_rule: Every meaningful semantic visual must either map to an approved upstream asset/reference class, be native presentation geometry, be an explicitly allowed raster role, or be classified as a profile-permitted novel illustration. Reject decorative or off-profile novel visuals.

novel_illustrations.guidance: Prefer native presentation geometry and approved assets. Allow a small number of semantically necessary illustrative visuals when they materially clarify a concept or create a justified narrative moment. Creative/conceptual slides may use more expressive illustration; compliance, regulatory, operating, or data-dense slides should use little or none. Do not add decorative novelty merely to fill space.

composition_freedom: Choose the visual composition, grouping structure, exact object placement, connector arrangement, and emphasis system that best communicates the semantic intent.
Do not force a fixed template, grid, card count, chart archetype, component precedent, or one icon treatment when another composition better supports the slide.
Preserve compositional freedom without relaxing resolved design values, profile hard rules, content, asset, or canvas constraints.
Density is a separate user/session control. Apply the selected density inside the profile rather than equating the profile with sparse or dense composition.

content.purpose: A dense five-page executive argument with consistent recurring typography, table treatment and decision bands. The Agent chooses and visually calibrates these values across the deck.

claim_title.guidance: One line at the same apparent size on all five content pages. Use the authored concise title. Begin near x48/y32 in the substantive canvas. Do not independently shrink a long title.

subtitle.guidance: A single supporting line under the title. Keep a comparable gap and one thin neutral divider under the introduction on every page.

section_heading.guidance: Compact uppercase section labels, visually distinct from the larger Georgia claim title.

table.body: Black regular text, with accountable row labels bold. Thin #DFE3E6 rules and white or #F5F7F8 rows.
table.emphasis: Use #FFF5ED for an intentionally selected row. Reserve #FD5108 text for its key data or explicit action.
table.guidance: Keep table header and body sizes consistent across the opportunity, responsibility, roadmap and investment tables. Do not stretch text.

data_highlight.guidance: Large opening KPIs may use a larger display role. Ordinary body text remains black.

decision_band.guidance: Use the same wide, shallow substantive conclusion band near the bottom of every page. Give the uppercase label a consistent left column and the message its own aligned column. No surrounding border, shadows, extra footnote strip or decorative rule. This band carries this page's decision and is not the shared footer.

connectors.guidance: Clear directional arrowheads with continuous routes. Lines explain relationships.

supporting_stage_icon.purpose: Help readers distinguish recurring actors, stages, workflows, and decisions before reading supporting text.

chosen_style.variant: line unless post-generation review supports a separate peer group
chosen_style.surface: transparent or #FFF5ED only when the accepted design uses a real surface

supporting_stage_icon.guidance: Icons support labels and evidence. Use one treatment within each local peer group and preserve the canonical SVG during reconstruction.

allowed_variations: Use KPI reasoning, chart-and-table comparison, a responsibility workflow, a roadmap matrix and an investment model as five different page compositions.
Vary the diagram and data geometry according to the argument while preserving recurring roles.
The opening has large numeric KPIs. This does not change the shared title, subtitle or decision-band typography.
cross_slide_review_focus: Generated images contain only the 1920 by 960 substantive canvas, with no header, footer, page number or company chrome.
Georgia claim titles retain the same apparent size, weight and single-line rhythm.
Arial subtitles, body copy, table text and section labels retain their respective peer sizes.
Every decision band uses the same pale orange fill, orange label, black message and left orange bar.
The final PowerPoint uses one shared inherited frame with the same neutral header and footer rules.
The Agent compares all five actual rendered pages together and corrects observed drift before release.
Selected icons remain recognizable, semantically useful, canonical in PowerPoint, and consistent within each peer group.
